newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela confident of peaceful solution in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Mandela confident of peaceful solution in Zaire.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Thursday he was confident of a peaceful solution to the civil war in Zaire.

"I have been speaking both to (rebel) president (Laurent) Kabila and to (Zairean) President Mobutu, and as a result of the exchanges I have had with them, and the other leaders in Africa, I am confident that a peaceful solution will be achieved," Mandela told reporters.
Mandela, who held an hour-long session on Wednesday evening with Kabila, said he had also spoken to Mobutu three times since last Saturday.

Mobutu's representative in an earlier round of talks in South Africa, Honore Ngbanda, had also been in the country, Mandela said, adding he had met Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo and his deputy Aziz Pahad.
Mandela said South Africa had flown Ngbanda back to Zaire on Thursday, where he was expected to consult Mobutu.

Earlier, foreign affairs officials said Kabila was also returning to Zaire on Thursday after making progress in Wednesday night's talks with Mandela and U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun, who have taken on the task of bringing peace to the troubled Central African country, half of which is now controlled by rebels.
